observation_summary: The loop in StrBuilder.deleteAll uses the index returned by indexOf(str, index) to perform deletions. After a deletion, the buffer size changes, but the index is not correctly validated or adjusted for the next iteration, leading to an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in System.arraycopy within deleteImpl.
hypothesis: The method StrBuilder.deleteAll (and similarly replaceAll) incorrectly updates the search index after a deletion. When deleteImpl is called, the size of the buffer decreases, but the subsequent call to indexOf(str, index) uses the old index, which may now point to an invalid position or skip occurrences because the string has shifted. The ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException occurs because the index passed to deleteImpl is not correctly adjusted relative to the new buffer size after previous deletions.
prediction: The loop in deleteAll will continue to use the same index or an incorrectly incremented index, causing it to attempt to delete from a position that is no longer valid or to pass an invalid range to deleteImpl.
experiment_rationale: The code snippet shows that after deleteImpl is called, the index is updated via index = indexOf(str, index). If the string was found at the end of the buffer or if the buffer size was reduced such that the index is now out of bounds, the next call to indexOf or deleteImpl will fail. This is a classic boundary/validation error in a loop condition.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure to correctly validate and update the loop state (the index) after a destructive operation (deleteImpl) modifies the underlying data structure. This is a Checking defect because the logic fails to ensure the index remains valid for the next iteration of the search.
